Subject: Tenant-scoped debug log retention exception request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CortexRx is moving toward a limited production pilot and our compliance team has a hard requirement to retain tenant debug/troubleshooting logs for 180 days for a small set of test tenants (we have a regulatory submission window tied to the pilot).

Specifically we're asking: can Redwood apply a per-tenant retention window of 180 days for these tenant IDs (I can provide the list once we sign the NDA amendment)? We also need documented evidence for SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ that shows:
- ability to apply tenant-scoped retention policies (separate from platform default)
- proof-of-delete workflow (audit manifest that shows deletes for a tenant)
- controls around export/access for those retained logs

Attached: cortexrx_retention_requirements.pdf (PDF)

Can you let us know what evidence you can provide and whether this requires a contract amendment or any operational carveouts? We prefer a short call to align.

Thanks,
Laura Shepherd

Hi Laura / Kimberly — quick technical note from infra:

We partition logs by tenant-id at ingestion and tag objects with tenant metadata. That lets us apply per-tenant TTLs at the storage layer without changing the global default. Implementation details:
- Retention enforcement: object lifecycle policies keyed by tenant tag; deletion executed by background reconciler with audit manifest generation.
- Proof-of-delete: we can produce a signed manifest (UTC timestamps + object keys) and a SHA256 snapshot hash for the deleted objects.
- Export options: we can produce a redacted export (PII redacted) or verbatim export under a secured transfer (SFTP/secure drive) depending on your contract.
- Operational caveat: extending retention for a small set of tenants increases our storage footprint; for pilot scale this is negligible, but at scale we'd propose a reserved-capacity addon to cover predictable storage.

If CortexRx needs immutable retention (WORM) for the 180d window, we can enable a tenant-level WORM bucket as a short-term solution (requires a brief configuration change and security review).

Happy to demo the proof-of-delete manifest format — I can include an example in the call.

— Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
